candidates.changed_node: the TS_MIN/TS_MAX extremum anchors (all three replaced by TS_MEAN)
candidates.rationale: Weakness is secular IC decay, 0.0250 in 2000 to 0.0010 in 2013, with stability 1.00 and a healthy 19.3-day half-life: the signal is not broken, it is crowded. The component responsible is the pair of single-print extremum anchors TS_MIN($low,21) and TS_MAX($high,21), which is the published stochastic/%R form every screen already runs. Replacing all three extremum estimators with TS_MEAN keeps the same anchor-and-normalise idea but reads support and resistance off the typical day rather than one spike, and it changes what the factor measures: (close - mean low) / (mean high - mean low) is displacement expressed in average daily ranges, an unbounded volatility-normalised position rather than a bounded [0,1] oscillator, so names with identical channel position but different range width now separate. Both parent blocks had to go regardless: $close - TS_MIN($low,21) is a 4-node subtree of this parent and TS_MAX($high,21) - TS_MIN($low,21) is a 7-node one, and a window rescale was not available (the 126-day twin was already logged as a duplicate and the $open/5-day variant screened at |t| 0.43). Three relabels, no other node touched. TS_MEAN($high,21) and TS_MEAN($low,21) each appear in the archive only as 3-node blocks, under the gate.

candidates.changed_node: TS_SUM($return, 5), with ABS inserted around the return leaf
candidates.rationale: Weakness is decay plus cost, not regime: IC half-life 4.3 days and one-way turnover 0.204, the highest in this set, against a fundamental leg whose own half-life is over 40 days. The component responsible is TS_SUM($return, 5), a signed one-week reversal that is fully spent inside a week and re-ranks the book every day to collect it. Inserting ABS converts that leg from a directional return aggregate into a short-horizon realised-movement state: volatility is persistent, so the leg re-ranks on a monthly rather than weekly clock, turnover should fall sharply and half-life lengthen, while the quality leg is left byte-identical. Directional return aggregates are also the documented weak family on this island, and the quality-minus-dispersion pairing is the strong one: an archived CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 10)) reached 0.01348 mean IC, above this parent. Lengthening the window instead is closed off, RANK($roa) - RANK(TS_SUM($return, 21)) came back rho 0.814 and the downside-clipped variant screened at |t| 0.02. One node inserted; TS_SUM(ABS($return), 5) is a 4-node block and the archive holds this shape only at windows 10, 21 and 63.

candidates.changed_node: $volume, wrapped as TS_DELTA($volume, 10) inside the correlation
candidates.rationale: Weakness is a regime problem, 2003 at -0.0057 is the only negative year and it sits in the price leg, not the quality leg. The component responsible is the raw $volume level as the correlation's first input: share volume has a strong secular trend across 2000-2013, so a level-versus-range correlation is partly measuring shared drift and its cross-sectional meaning inverts when the volatility regime turns. A 10-day change strips the level and asks whether volume surprises land on wide bars, which is the price-impact effect the kernel is meant to price and is regime-neutral by construction. The correlation block had to change anyway: TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 15) is a 6-node subtree of this parent, so no wrapper-only or window-only edit was legal. Two edits, both inside the volume argument; the quality lead and the range leg stay byte-identical. TS_DELTA($volume, 10) is a 3-node block and the archive's only $volume delta is at window 1 in a 21-day correlation, so the 8-node correlation is new.

Weakness is a dead modulator. 63 trading days spans a single filing gap, so a one-sided clip of that difference is exactly zero for most names on most days and the leverage term switches off across the cross-section; that is why the nearest archive neighbour already sits at rho 0.794, and why 2003 at -0.0069 is the worst year here, a market-wide deleveraging year in which MAX(dLeverage, 0) was zero almost everywhere. A 126-day window spans two filings and a full financing decision, so the clip stays dispersed and the modulator earns its free constant. The correlation's range input had to move with it because TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42) is a 6-node subtree of this parent and MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 0) is a 5-node one, so both blocks are forced; the 10-day range change is the archive-free variant of the transform that already carried an accept at 5 days, and it keeps the leg regime-neutral. Total lookback stays at 126. Coverage should land near 0.93, in line with the archived 126-day leverage delta at 0.932. Three edits: one window literal, one node inserted, one literal for it.

Weakness is a redundant leg carrying the 2003 failure (-0.0086, the worst year in this set) and 0.200 of complexity charge for five fields. The component responsible is $dollar_volume / ($open + 1e-8): dividing dollar volume by a raw price just recovers share volume, and those two collapse into each other at rho 0.99 in this exact kernel, so the guarded division buys a fifth field and nothing else while leaving a non-stationary volume level as the correlation's second series. Swapping the divisor to $volume turns the same ratio into the day's average execution price on the raw scale, so the correlation becomes range-versus-price-level: whether a name's intraday range widens as it re-prices, an asymmetric-volatility state rather than a size and liquidity sort. Renormalising against volume's own history is closed off, the TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) version came back rho 0.917, precisely because any own-history baseline leaves the leg dominated by the same volume level; a price series does not. One leaf edit. $dollar_volume / ($volume + 1e-8) is a 5-node block absent from the archive, which also clears the parent's 10-node correlation. Windows and coverage are untouched at 0.959.

candidates.changed_node: $high in the range leg, making it $open - $low
candidates.rationale: Weakness is the lowest stability in the set, 0.86, with the two negative years falling in 2003 (-0.0051) and 2013 (-0.0013), the two calmest tapes in the window. The component responsible is the symmetric range $high - $low: in a quiet year most of that range is bid-ask bounce and gap noise rather than absorbed order flow, so the correlation stops measuring price impact and its sign is not stable. Restricting the second series to $open - $low keeps only the downside half of the bar, where liquidation and forced supply show up; volume that arrives while price is pushed below the open is liquidity demand being absorbed, and that is the effect this kernel is paid for, whereas volume arriving with upside extension is information and is not. The prior five mutations of this parent all rebuilt the volume leg (deltas, time-series ranks, dollar volume); the range leg has only ever been touched once, as $high - $open, so the downside half is untried. One leaf edit, and it is forced anyway since TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 21) is a 6-node subtree of this parent. $open - $low appears in the archive only as a 3-node fragment, under the gate; coverage and turnover are unchanged.

Weakness is decay: IC half-life 4.7 days against 18.2 for the same kernel without the delta, bought with turnover 0.122 and a dead 2013 (+0.0002). The component responsible is the unbounded 5-day difference of a dollar-volume level, which is set by one or two spike days, so the 21-day correlation is effectively estimated off a handful of outliers and has nothing left to say by the end of the week. Ranking that difference inside its own 42-day history keeps the flow-surprise idea but bounds it and makes it persistent, so the correlation becomes a slow state rather than a spike detector; half-life should lengthen toward the 18-day family norm and turnover fall. This attacks the same named weakness the two earlier mutations did but by a different route: they lengthened the delta to 21 days and swapped the delta for a level rank at a 63-day correlation, both of which are archived, whereas bounding the innovation itself while leaving the correlation window and the range leg byte-identical is untried. Two edits, one node and one literal. TS_RANK(TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5), 42) is a 5-node block absent from the archive, so the parent's 8-node correlation is cleared. Total lookback 68 days.

candidates.changed_node: the * combinator joining the two legs, changed to -
candidates.rationale: Weakness is that the price leg does almost no work: half-life 57.1 days and turnover 0.029, the slowest and cheapest here, because a non-negative multiplier on a centred quality rank barely disturbs the quality ordering. That is a measured property of this family, not a guess: a sibling multiplier swap on this same lead scored rho 0.98 against it, and a $roa version of exactly this shape was rejected at rho 0.930 against the bare RANK($roa). So the multiplicative combinator, not either leg, is the weakest component; under a difference of cross-sectional ranks the price leg finally carries equal weight, which is also what breaks the factor's dependence on the quality tilt that fails in 2003 (-0.0035). The range estimator had to move with it because the 11-node CS_RANK(TS_MEAN($high - $low, 10) / (TS_MEAN($open, 10) + 1e-8)) is a complete subtree of this parent; TS_STD rather than TS_MEAN also changes the leg from a static relative-volatility level into range instability, which re-ranks and keeps it away from the archived roe-minus-range-percentile member. Two edits: one operator relabel at the root, one inside the numerator. TS_STD($high - $low, 10) is a 5-node block absent from the archive.

candidates.changed_node: $roa in the first leg, replaced by $operating_margin
candidates.rationale: Weakness is that this factor is essentially its first leg. Two prior rebuilds of the second leg's price modulator, swapping TS_MAX($high, 21) for TS_MAX($high, 126) and for TS_STD($high, 21), both came back at rho 0.92 against this parent, which is direct evidence the fundamental rank sets the ranking and the leverage-times-price term is near-inert. So the weakest component is $roa: it makes the first leg a balance-sheet profitability tilt, and 2003 (-0.0034) is the standard junk-rally year in which that tilt pays nothing. Moving to $operating_margin sources quality from the income statement instead, which is the swap that actually creates distance, unlike $roa to $roe, which collides at rho 0.859. The TS_MAX window had to move with it because TS_MAX($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8) is a 6-node subtree of this parent and CS_RANK($roa - $accrual_gap) is a 4-node one, so both blocks are forced; 42 is chosen because TS_MEAN($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8) is itself an archived block. Two edits, one leaf and one literal. Coverage should sit near 0.94, in line with archived $operating_margin members.

Weakness is coverage: 0.912 against a 0.90 floor, the tightest margin in this set. The component responsible is TS_RANK($close, 168), which burns 168 trading days of warmup, well past this island's 126-day lookback ceiling, and buys a slow price-level percentile that cannot be the source of this factor's 3.8-day IC half-life; the fast fundamental delta is doing the predicting while the price gate is paying the panel cost. Cutting the window to 126 returns roughly forty trading days of panel and keeps the conditioning claim intact, that the accrual charge bites hardest in names that have already re-rated. Note the earlier attempt at this window failed coverage at 0.883 only because it simultaneously moved the delta to $asset_turnover, which is the sparse field, so the window itself was never tested. The first leg's field had to move because CS_ZSCORE(TS_DELTA($roa, 63)) is a 4-node subtree of this parent and both CS_RANK($roa, 63) and the $asset_turnover delta are spent archive blocks; margin change is the remaining accounting axis and carries standalone signal. Two edits, both literals or leaves; the accrual leg is untouched. Fields drop to three.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Directional return aggregates buy almost nothing. SIGN sums, TS_MEAN/TS_STD sharpe forms, TS_ARGMAX(ABS($return),63) and summed raw OHLC gaps produced the three weakest accepts (0.382, 0.591, 0.603). Dispersion, concentration and correlation kernels produced everything above 1.9.
  2. CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) as a leading term is spent: in one round it drew both a 5-node archive_subtree hit and a rho 0.901 correlation hit against the same archive member. CS_ZSCORE or plain CS_RANK on $accrual_gap and $asset_turnover carried the 3.1 to 4.1 accepts.
  3. Rescaling a window is not a decorrelating edit. The 126-day channel-position kernel came back rho 0.858 against its 21-day twin. Spend mutation edits on replacing a whole leg; the one non-local reject wasted its budget scattering edits across wrapper, leg and window at once.
  4. Keep total lookback at 126 days or less. A DELAY($close,189) leg was the round's only coverage failure at 0.896; every expression at 126 or below cleared the gate, including 126-day TS_CORR.
